name: MicroBooNE
summary: MicroBooNE is a completed Fermilab liquid-argon neutrino exposure whose analyses test the MiniBooNE low-energy excess and provide extensive neutrino-argon interaction measurements.
physics_targets: Nature of the MiniBooNE low-energy excess
Neutrino-argon differential and exclusive cross sections
Sterile neutrinos, dark sectors and detector methods
detection_principle: Three wire planes measure ionization electrons drifting through liquid argon, while optical detectors time the interaction. Fine imaging distinguishes single electrons from converted photons by their initial ionization and event topology.

results.summary: The collaboration continues to publish low-energy-excess and cross-section analyses from its completed exposure; exclusion results depend on the signal model tested.

Combined the on-axis Booster and off-axis NuMI beam samples in a light-sterile-neutrino oscillation search. The constraints apply to the tested mixing model and parameter region; they do not exclude every possible sterile-neutrino scenario.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
